newsitem.title: THAILAND: Moody's reaffirms no plans to review Thai rating.
newsitem.headline: Moody's reaffirms no plans to review Thai rating.

text.p: U.S. rating agency Moody's Investor Services reaffirmed that it has no current plans to review Thailand's sovereign debt rating, a senior Moody's executive told a conference on Asian debt on Monday.
"I'm not aware of any plans to take any action on the Thai rating," Moody's Japan Managing Director Julia Turner said.
The rating agency downgraded Thailand's long term sovereign status to A3 from A2 in April in reaction to a number of concerns surrounding the Thai economy.

Recent moves to float the currency which has effectively devalued the baht by around 15 percent and a possibility the Thai government may issue $5-10 billion more debt were not necessarily reasons for a further ratings review, she said.
"The world knows the issues that concern us because we published them in the recent actions," she said.

In April the agency said it was concerned by the build up of short term foreign currency obligations, slowing export growth, constraints on the effectiveness of Thailand's economic policy, and crises in the financial and property sectors.
Moody's executives in New York last week said the agency had anticipated the baht's de facto devaluation and would not be taking any action purely on this issue.
